page: Microsoft Azure E96-24as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features a constrained core configuration delivering 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It provides 672.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 28.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server includes no integrated GPUs and provides no bundled local ephemeral storage, relying on network-attached storage for disk operations.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate performance characteristics aligned with its memory-centric architecture. In memory benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results in the PassMark memory suite, landing in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, alongside 24.18 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Compute metrics show strong single-core execution in stress-ng (top 25 percent) and a Geekbench single-core score of 1724.0, while multi-core compute metrics such as the multi-core stress-ng score of 32380.27 and PassMark CPU score of 31301.33 remain within the median 50 percent range, bounded by the 24-vCPU allocation.

From an efficiency perspective, the E96-24as_v5 configuration offers qualitative cost advantages for software environments priced on a per-core licensing model. By maintaining 672.0 GB of RAM while restricting active compute to 24 vCPUs, it reduces hypervisor and application licensing overheads that would otherwise scale to 96 cores. Workloads fitting this profile include commercial relational database management systems, large in-memory caching tiers, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-intensive analytics pipelines that require vast memory capacity without requiring 96 processor cores.
